summary: Anil Vidyalankar is a scholar in linguistics and philosophy who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, where he earned his PhD. He founded Sandhaan in 1988 and served as its director (attested 1999).

Ankur Barua works in Buddhist studies and other fields. He earned degrees from the Manipal Academy of Higher Education (MD, 2003), Sikkim Manipal University (MBAIT, 2007), and the University of Hong Kong (MBuddStud, 2009), and held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned a Master of Arts at the Australian National University (attested 1983), where she studied under supervisors Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus.
Ann Gleig is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at Rice University, studying under doctoral supervisor Jeffrey J. Kripal.

Ann Grodzins Gold is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1975–1984). She held posts at Cornell University (~1988–1993) and Syracuse University, where she became Professor of Religion and Anthropology around 1993.

Ann Heirman is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1995–2009) and Ghent University (2003–2012), where around 2000 she served as professor of Chinese language and culture and head of the Centre for Buddhist Studies.

Ann Laura Stoler works in history, archaeology, and other fields. After studying at Columbia University (~1974–1982), she held posts at the University of Michigan (1989–2003) and The New School (2004).

Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indology scholar who earned an MA at the University of Tübingen (1998) and studied at Heidelberg University. She held a post as Assistant Professor of Indology at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015).

Anna Balikci Denjongpa is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned her PhD at SOAS University of London under Lionel Caplan, also studying with traditional teachers Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku. In 2002, she became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields is a Sinology scholar who held positions at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015) and Princeton University (~2015).

Anna Madelyn Hennessey is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2011), where she studied under doctoral supervisor William F. Powell.

Anna Sawerthal is a Tibetologist who earned an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes and a PhD at Heidelberg University under Birgit Kellner and Roland Wenzlhuemer. Her teachers also include Johanna Buß, Dawa Tsering, and Norbu Tashi.
Anna Seidel was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Maxime Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein between approximately 1961 and 1968.
Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University (1972–1976). She held academic posts at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1990–1999) and New York University (~1999).

Anna-Pya Sjödin is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed her PhD at Uppsala University in 2007. Her doctoral supervisors were Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, and her teachers included Klas Hagren and Barbro Eriksson.

Anne Carolyn Klein is a Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies scholar who studied at Binghamton University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and the University of Virginia. She held posts at Harvard University and Rice University, and co-founded the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism.

Anne Casile is an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. She worked as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (~2008–2011) and held a post at the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (~2011).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Harvard University (~1989–1997) under Diana L. Eck and Kausalya Hart. She taught at the University of Virginia (~1997–2002) and became professor of South Asian religions at Harvard in 2002.

Anne Feldhaus is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Manhattanville University (~1967–1971) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). She took up a post at Arizona State University around 1981.
